findings.routeWitness: barrelInspection.coverBarrel -> barrelSetAside -> barrelWasNotCauseWell or barrelWasNotCauseDebris -> wrongSource. The preceding effects set barrelClosed only; wrongSource variants claim the well was closed, with wellDebris text also claiming its channel is being cleared.
findings.violatedRule: Investigation and containment state in converged text must match actions actually taken on the selected route.

findings.defect: The hold-for-claim ending asserts that the folding rule has a missing brass hinge pin, although the setup explicitly says its brass hinge moves freely and no route establishes the pin is missing.
findings.routeWitness: stall (brass hinge moves freely) -> sellerAccount.askMarketKeeper or markSeen.holdAfterMark -> heldForClaim (requires claimant to describe a missing brass hinge pin).
findings.violatedRule: Object condition at a later scene must remain compatible with explicit setup and route-established state.

findings.defect: Gear-use choices accept a BROKEN item because they check ownership only, allowing the player to use tools that the engine considers unusable.
findings.routeWitness: roadsideWork.takePaidWork -> paidWorksite.useMultiTool/useFoldingRule; roadsideWork.helpForPassage -> volunteerWorksite.volunteerWithTool/volunteerWithRule. Each use choice requires `items` but omits `usableItems`; `engine.ts` defines `items` as inventory inclusion and rejects BROKEN gear only under `usableItems`.
findings.violatedRule: An action requiring functioning Gear must gate on usability, not ownership alone.

findings.defect: Both Travel Rope crossing actions accept a BROKEN rope because their requirements test ownership only.
findings.routeWitness: nearBank.useTravelRope or searchDownstream -> downstreamShelf.handlineCross; both require `items: ['travelRope']` without `usableItems`. The engine's `items` check admits the still-owned BROKEN rope, though each action relies on it holding/steadying the crossing.
findings.violatedRule: A broken tool must not be treated as functioning route proof or equipment.

findings.defect: Setting a lantern deterministically reaches an ending that asserts an unestablished traveler answers and accompanies the Traveler.
findings.routeWitness: foggyTrack.signalLantern -> heardTravelers. The choice only sets a history flag and says the light may help someone; no participant/arrival state is established, yet the ending says a traveler answers and both proceed together. The scenario's `alone` roadBend variant also says no other traveler answers the call.
findings.violatedRule: Optional participant presence and response must be established before shared text claims participation.

findings.defect: The trail-marker placement choice is available with a BROKEN marker because it checks inventory ownership only.
findings.routeWitness: dryHollow.changeTomorrowRoute -> morningRoute. The choice requires `items: ['foldingTrailMarker']` but not `usableItems`; engine semantics allow an owned BROKEN marker to satisfy the requirement even though the ending says it is hung to mark the route.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of Gear requires a usable item, not mere inventory ownership.

findings.defect: A BROKEN Signal Mirror can still establish a successful signal and reply from the distant trail crew.
findings.routeWitness: twoRoutes.signalFromFork (requires items only) -> signalSeen, which says the crew sees the mirror and signals back; engine `items` checks ownership while `usableItems` rejects BROKEN gear.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of Gear requires a usable item, not mere inventory ownership.

findings.defect: After inspecting existing marks, the Traveler can hang a BROKEN Folding Trail Marker.
findings.routeWitness: markedJunction.inspectMarks -> marksInspected.markJunctionAfterLook (items only) -> ownMarkPlaced, which says the marker hangs and records the stopping point; the initial hangOwnMarker route correctly requires usableItems.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of Gear requires a usable item, not mere inventory ownership.

findings.defect: After-dark travel and warming choices accept owned BROKEN light/blanket gear as functional.
findings.routeWitness: longRoadEvening.continueWithLantern requires only `items: ['roadmansLantern']` and can reach lateArrival, which says the lantern made the road possible; campedKnoll.useBlanket checks anyItems rather than anyUsableItems and reaches warmCamp. The Windproof Match Case route correctly requires a usable item.
findings.violatedRule: A route action depending on functioning Gear must require usability; broken gear cannot establish light or warmth.

findings.defect: The Traveler can attempt the calf rescue using a BROKEN Travel Rope.
findings.routeWitness: muddyGate.prepareRopePull checks only `items`; ropeReady.ropeWithHandler also has no `usableItems` requirement and can resolve to calfFree or pauseCalf. The glove variant correctly requires a usable rope; farmhand-supplied rope and board routes are independent.
findings.violatedRule: A physically used rescue tool must be usable; owned-but-broken gear is not functional route proof.

findings.defect: The no-person/no-object dog variant can converge on an ending that narrates absent interventions and says the dog helped someone notice a need.
findings.routeWitness: dogReason=nothing -> dogFollowed -> dogTruth (nothing appears lost or injured) -> offerPracticalHelp -> dogHelped; the ending has no dogReason-specific variant.
findings.violatedRule: Converged narration must not import participants, objects, or interventions absent from the selected route.

findings.defect: Successful relocation of the mule to the stable claims two ownership claimants are comparing accounts when no claimant was established.
findings.routeWitness: muleGreen.inspectMuleTack -> muleClueSeen.leadMuleStable success -> muleAtStable; this bypasses muleClaimant, while the shared ending says two claimants compare their accounts.
findings.violatedRule: Shared outcome text may assert only participants and facts established by every incoming route.

findings.defect: The Traveler can steady a hive stand with a BROKEN tool because the action checks inventory presence rather than usability.
findings.routeWitness: apiaryGate.steadyStandTool requires anyItems from pocketToolkit/foremanMultiTool/gateHook, then sets apiaryStandLeveled and enters standSteadied. Engine anyItems checks inventory only; anyUsableItems filters BROKEN gear.
findings.violatedRule: Physical Gear use requires a usable item, not merely an item present in inventory.

findings.defect: The ask-creek-name route records Knowledge that a name was shared although the converged conversation provides only a geographic description, no name.
findings.routeWitness: fishingResult.askCreekName -> fishingTalk. The effect says a local angler shared the creek bend's name and nearby footpath; fishingTalk says only that it bends around an alder stand before meeting the old footpath.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge entries must not claim a specific fact that the route's dialogue does not actually convey.

findings.defect: The no-curiosity variant still allows a keepsake action and records a kept object that does not exist.
findings.routeWitness: shoreCuriosity=nothing -> poolBank.lookPoolShore -> poolShore text says nothing to find -> keepPoolCuriosity (ungated) sets kept_a_small_swimming_hole_curiosity and reaches poolKeepsake claiming a stone or smoothed glass was pocketed.
findings.violatedRule: Choices and persistent route history must not claim possession/recovery when the selected route established that no object was found.

clusters.name: Route-specific state lost at convergence
clusters.description: Route-specific location, outcome, person/helper, object, method, or prior-intervention facts are lost at convergence, causing shared scenes/endings to assert facts not established by every incoming route.

clusters.name: Knowledge/History without route proof
clusters.description: Knowledge and/or History is granted without sufficient route proof that the Traveler actually learned or established it.

clusters.name: Elapsed-time proxy used as event proof
clusters.description: Elapsed time is used as a proxy for a specific event/consequence, making later narration claim that event on routes where it did not occur.

clusters.name: Gear ownership treated as Gear usability
clusters.description: Choices that physically use Gear check only that it remains in inventory, allowing BROKEN gear to satisfy the action requirement instead of requiring usableItems.
